{"meetingId": "Nadia Pebblefizz met by video with lead financial advisor Mira Quillwhistle, associate advisor and planning analyst Tobin Mossbutton, and client service manager and operations coordinator Elena Cloudpuddle of Pocket Lantern Advisory on 2025-02-11 for an education funding review. Nadia is married to Owen Pebblefizz, and they file a joint federal tax return. They have two children, Lila Pebblefizz and Jonah Pebblefizz. Lila is a high school senior who has accepted admission to Buttonwood Balloon University for the fall 2025 academic year. Jonah is a high school sophomore, and the household expects his college search to begin in 2026.

Buttonwood Balloon University estimated Lila’s first-year cost of attendance at $79,400, including tuition, required fees, housing, meal plan, books, and travel. The university’s preliminary aid letter showed a $12,000 merit scholarship for Lila’s first year and no need-based grant in the initial award package. Nadia asked Pocket Lantern Advisory to map Lila’s expected first-year cost against the merit scholarship, the Lila 529 account, available checking cash, and any remaining gap so the household can see the order and timing of likely funding sources. The agreed follow-up is to prepare that first-year college funding schedule by 2025-02-21.

Nadia and Owen have a Velvet Acorn Custody 529 account for Lila valued at $103,800 as of 2025-02-07. At the time of the review, the Lila 529 account was invested about 70% in equity-oriented options and 30% in short-term bond and cash-equivalent options. The team noted that the account still had a large equity-oriented allocation despite the near-term tuition use, and the discussion covered preparing risk-reduction options before the next withdrawal decision. The agreed follow-up is to prepare the Lila 529 investment positioning review by 2025-02-24.

Nadia did not have the final university billing statement, itemized fee schedule, or complete financial aid portal export available during the meeting, and the analysis depends on the confirmed net amount owed after the scholarship. The agreed follow-up is to collect the university aid and billing documents by 2025-02-18. The university payment portal showed an accepted housing deposit, but Nadia’s printed student account statement did not show the credit. Nadia showed that the accepted housing deposit appeared in the portal but was absent from the printed statement, creating uncertainty about the remaining balance to fund. The agreed follow-up is to address the housing deposit credit mismatch by 2025-02-20.

Nadia has online access to the Lila 529 account, but Owen’s login attempt produced an identity-verification lockout during the week before the meeting. Nadia reported that Owen’s Velvet Acorn Custody login was locked after an identity-verification attempt, and the household wants both parents able to view the education account before withdrawal planning. The agreed follow-up is to address Owen’s locked 529 account access by 2025-02-17. Nadia and Owen also have a separate Velvet Acorn Custody 529 account for Jonah valued at $64,200 as of 2025-02-07, and the Jonah 529 account receives an automatic monthly contribution of $650 from Nadia and Owen’s joint checking account.

Nadia and Owen hold $42,500 in a Teacup Comet Bank high-yield savings account that they describe as their household emergency reserve. The household keeps a separate Teacup Comet Bank checking account with an ordinary month-end balance near $18,000 for regular bills. Nadia and Owen’s household spending averages about $15,600 per month before education expenses. They have stated that they prefer to avoid parent PLUS loans if they can cover Lila’s first two years with 529 assets, cash flow, scholarships, and limited taxable sales. They also want to preserve at least six months of core household expenses in cash while Lila is in college.

Nadia works as a product design director at Silver Marmot Robotics and earns a base salary of $218,000. Nadia’s Silver Marmot Robotics compensation package includes a target annual bonus of 18% of salary and restricted stock units that vest quarterly. Owen works as a project manager at Paper Otter Works and moved to a reduced four-day schedule in January 2025, lowering his annual salary from $142,000 to $112,000. Owen’s move to a four-day schedule reduced household salary income, and the education funding plan needs to reflect the lower recurring cash flow while preserving the stated emergency reserve preference. The agreed follow-up is to reflect the effect of Owen’s reduced work schedule on college cash flow by 2025-03-03. Nadia contributes 12% of pay to her 401(k), and Owen contributes 8% of pay to his workplace retirement plan.

Nadia and Owen own a home with an estimated market value of $910,000 and a remaining mortgage balance of about $438,000. Their mortgage payment is $3,840 per month, including taxes and insurance escrow. They also have a home equity line with a $120,000 limit and no current balance. Nadia requested a comparison of the university monthly payment plan, a home equity line draw, and a limited taxable brokerage sale for any first-year shortfall that remains after scholarship and 529 funding. The agreed follow-up is to prepare the payment plan and short-term borrowing comparison by 2025-03-10.

Nadia holds Silver Marmot Robotics stock worth about $286,000 in a taxable brokerage account at Velvet Acorn Custody. The Silver Marmot Robotics taxable position represented about 22% of Nadia and Owen’s investable assets at the time of the meeting. Nadia estimated the taxable Silver Marmot Robotics shares had an unrealized long-term gain of about $171,000. The review identified a sizeable taxable holding in Nadia’s employer stock, and Nadia asked for tax-aware sale scenarios that could fund part of Lila’s college shortfall without creating an unnecessarily large concentrated-position reduction at one time. The agreed follow-up is to prepare the Silver Marmot Robotics stock concentration and tuition funding scenarios by 2025-03-05.

Nadia’s mother, Iris Pebblefizz, gave Lila $8,000 during the prior winter break for college costs, and the funds remain in Nadia and Owen’s checking account. The household’s 2024 tax file did not yet include the relevant education-related statements for Lila’s dual-enrollment coursework or the record of Iris Pebblefizz’s college gift, and Nadia asked the team to coordinate the needed document list with the CPA. The agreed follow-up is to coordinate that needed tax document list with the CPA by 2025-02-19.

Nadia and Owen’s wills name each other as primary guardians for financial administration and name Nadia’s sister, Sera Bramblequill, as successor fiduciary for the children’s assets. Nadia said the 529 successor-owner fields were completed years ago, before Sera Bramblequill became the preferred successor fiduciary in the estate documents. Nadia also said the 529 successor-owner information may no longer align with the fiduciary named in the current estate documents, and she asked that the update process for the education accounts be coordinated.
